transcript.text: If a tumble dryer appears to run indefinitely, it is often because it is in the cool-down phase at the end of a cycle (the drum turns but no heat is applied) or the door switch has failed and the machine thinks the door is open so it keeps tumbling to prevent overheating. To help narrow this down: is the drum still turning and warm, or has it stopped tumbling but left the heater on? Also, does the door feel like it is clicking shut properly?
drum still turning a bit every couple of mins but clothes are cool, no heat. door shuts ok i think

The symptoms you describe—intermittent turning with cool clothes and no heat—are very typical of a tumble dryer entering its cool-down phase at the end of a cycle. Many machines continue to tumble slowly for 10–20 minutes after heating stops to prevent clothes from creasing. Please check if the display shows 'End', '0:00' or indicates the cycle is complete. If it has finished, this is normal behaviour and you can simply switch it off. If the cycle has not yet ended but there is no heat, please check the lint filter (usually located in the door opening) for blockages. A blocked filter can cause the machine to cut the heat as a safety precaution while still tumbling. Clean the filter thoroughly and try running the cycle again.
yes it says End. but the drum keeps turning every couple of mins for about an hour if i leave the clothes in. stops when i open the door. is that normal?

Yes, that is normal. Most tumble dryers have an anti-crease or cool-down phase at the end of a cycle where they tumble the clothes intermittently for up to 60 minutes to prevent them from setting in creases while still warm. Since the display says 'End' and the clothes are cool, this is just the machine doing its job. You can simply open the door to stop it immediately if you want to take the clothes out now.
